back: A forecast gives the probability of an event over a period. Early warning detects an event that has started and sends an alert before the damaging waves arrive.
Swarms of small earthquakes and tremor, ground swelling, rising sulfur dioxide and increased heat show that magma is moving up.
There is no reliable signal; scientists identify seismic gaps and give probabilities, and early warning gives only seconds.
Reinforced frames, cross-bracing, shear walls and base isolators let buildings sway without collapse; codes must be enforced and old buildings retrofitted.
Hazard maps and exclusion zones keep housing out of lahar channels and pyroclastic flow paths.
Monitoring and staged alerts led to the evacuation of tens of thousands; about 800 people died, many from roof collapse under wet ash during a typhoon.
Warning time = S wave arrival time (distance ÷ 3.5 km/s) − time of the alert.
How people judge a hazard, shaped by past experience, trust, education and the benefits of living there; it can differ from the real risk.
Search and rescue in the first days, then shelter, water, health care and rebuilding to safer standards; depends on wealth, insurance, aid and governance.
